task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Keep the documented retry budget unchanged, guard payment retries with idempotency, fit per-attempt timeouts and jittered backoff within that budget, improve connection reuse, and roll out with metrics and rollback.
plan_steps: Check stored retry, timeout, and idempotency records before setting any numeric values.
Instrument attempt count, per-attempt timeout, total elapsed time, and idempotency-key presence for payment requests.
Adjust connection reuse or pooling and per-attempt timeouts only within the documented attempts and overall budget, using jittered backoff between permitted attempts.
Roll out behind a flag with load testing and rollback based on timeout and duplicate-payment indicators.

claims.statement: A payment-creation request will be retried only if it carries an idempotency key; otherwise it will not be automatically resent.
The proposal does not add attempts beyond the documented maximum retry attempts for the payment client.
The sum of per-attempt timeouts and backoff delays for one payment request will not exceed the documented overall retry deadline or timeout budget for the payment client.

assumptions: Timeouts under load may involve connection-pool contention or downstream latency, so tuning pool reuse and per-attempt timeouts within the existing total budget may help; this cause is not established by the provided task text.
The payment service honors idempotency keys if they are already supported by the client and API.
uncertainties: The documented maximum retry attempts, per-attempt timeout, overall deadline, and backoff policy were not provided in the task text, so numeric compliance cannot be confirmed from the task alone.
Whether the payment client and API already support idempotency keys is not provided.
The root cause of the intermittent timeouts and the current load, pool, and downstream latency profile are not provided.

evidence.content: Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

items.description: Claim-3 is ambiguous and potentially contradictory because keeping the existing budget unchanged could retain the default max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0, while the documented decision requires max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and the existing test rejects jitter_ms equal to 0.

Claim-3 cannot be verified because the proposal specifies no concrete max_attempts or jitter_ms value, even though the documented constraint caps outbound retries at 3 attempts with jitter and the payments decision specifically requires jitter_ms of at least 50.

Claim-4 is unsupported because the proposal provides no per-attempt timeout value, backoff range, overall deadline value, or deadline-enforcement mechanism, and the retrieved records specify attempt and jitter limits without establishing a total timeout budget against which the summed delays could be checked.

Claim-2 rests on unverified idempotency support because no retrieved record shows that the payment client or API supports or honors idempotency keys, and the current send_with_retries behavior is described only as retrying Timeout errors up to max_attempts without any idempotency-key gate.

Claim-2 does not by itself prevent duplicate payments because instrumenting the presence of an idempotency key does not establish that the same key is reused across every retry of one payment or that the downstream service deduplicates requests using that key.

The proposal does not explicitly preserve the existing timeout-only retry scope, so a generic change to payment retries could start retrying upstream errors that send_with_retries currently returns immediately without a retry.

Claim-3's attempt cap alone does not address the documented retry-burst regression risk because the proposal specifies no minimum jitter value, retry rate limit, circuit breaker, or quantitative rollback threshold despite evidence that payment-client retry bursts amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

The proposal's load-testing plan omits the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test and any explicit verification that max_attempts stays at or below 3 while jitter_ms is non-zero and at least 50.

assessments.note: No Valid record directly states an idempotency-key retry gate, support or honoring of keys, same-key reuse across retries, or downstream deduplication; the proposal only instruments key presence.

No Valid record directly states the proposal's concrete max_attempts or jitter_ms or that it stays within the cap; records establish a cap but also a default of max_attempts=1, jitter_ms=0 conflicting with required jitter, leaving compliance unsettled.

No Valid record establishes an overall retry deadline or total timeout budget, and the proposal provides no per-attempt timeout, backoff range, deadline value, or enforcement mechanism to check the sum.

proposal.summary: Set the payment-client RetryPolicy to the documented decision values max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50, replacing the default 1 and 0, while preserving timeout-only retry scope; unsupported idempotency and total-deadline claims are removed.
plan_steps: Change the payment-client RetryPolicy from max_attempts=1, jitter_ms=0 to max_attempts=3, jitter_ms=50; do not raise max_attempts above 3.
Preserve the existing send_with_retries scope: retry only SendError::Timeout and return upstream errors immediately without retry.
Run the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test and verify max_attempts is at or below 3, jitter_ms is non-zero, and jitter_ms is at least 50 before rollout.
Do not add an idempotency-gated retry expansion or claim duplicate-payment prevention until stored records verify idempotency-key support, same-key reuse across retries, and downstream deduplication.
Do not change per-attempt timeouts or assert a total retry-deadline budget, because no cited record establishes an overall deadline or per-attempt timeout budget.

Roll out behind a flag with load testing, monitor attempts per request and timeout indicators, and roll back if constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails, jitter_ms falls below 50, or any request exceeds 3 attempts.

claims.statement: The payment-client RetryPolicy will be changed from the documented default max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50.
Retry scope will remain limited to SendError::Timeout via send_with_retries up to max_attempts; upstream errors will be returned immediately without retry.

assumptions: A transient SendError::Timeout may succeed on a subsequent attempt within the 3-attempt cap; effectiveness under current load is not established by the cited records.
uncertainties: No cited record establishes an overall retry deadline, per-attempt timeout value, or total timeout budget, so total-budget compliance cannot be verified.
No cited record establishes idempotency-key support, same-key reuse across retries, or downstream deduplication.
Whether jitter_ms=50 is sufficient to prevent retry bursts under current load, and the current latency and load profile, are not established by the cited records.

items.description: The existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test does not enforce the exact rollout configuration because it passes with max_attempts below 3 and with jitter_ms between 1 and 49, while the decision requires max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms of at least 50 and the proposal adds no automated test for those exact values.

The proposal names only the cap-and-jitter test as verification, so it provides no stated regression test proving that after the policy change send_with_retries still retries only SendError::Timeout and returns upstream errors immediately without retry.

Retrying a payment request after SendError::Timeout up to three attempts without verified idempotency-key reuse or downstream deduplication creates a duplicate-payment risk if a timed-out attempt was already processed downstream, and the stated monitoring covers attempts and timeout indicators but not duplicate charges.

The proposal defines no load-test acceptance threshold and no rollback trigger based on retry-burst rate or upstream load, so it does not close the documented risk that payment-client retry bursts can amplify an upstream slowdown into an outage even with jitter_ms=50.

Increasing max_attempts from one to three can extend a request across up to three attempts, but the proposal sets no total retry deadline or latency-based rollback threshold and admits that no cited record establishes a per-attempt or total timeout budget against which the longer duration can be checked.

assessments.note: Default 1/0 and decision 3/at-least-50 are directly stated in valid records.
Timeout-only retry and immediate upstream-error return are directly stated in a valid record.
